title: The Long Haul

source.title: Sky-high gas prices aren't shaking Trump's MAGA faithful in oil country as supporters warn of bigger threat
source.note: published 10-29 13:35 ET; the 10-29 sweep (matched on 'gasoline', 'midterm', 'venezuela'). Fox's station on the roster is 'RI?' — proposed, ruling owed; scored as RI on the 10-20/21/23/24/27 precedents, flag on the figure. Read in full via the cloud fetch; reductions filed, no quotation over twelve words. A rally page: the article, four voters, the White House as reported, and the holder, from Lubbock and Corpus Christi (the rallies undated on the page; the price dated to Wednesday 10-28). The newest Fox hit on the live object; chosen over the Fox Power Rankings update (10-29 09:00, South Carolina to toss-up — the slate), the Libertarians page (Iran once, as Joe Kent's reason) and the Houthi/WFP page (the force's edge, no price); my call

object.label: H1 — the Russian diesel deal (PG01 layer 1): the price leg (H1c) at the pump, read at two Texas rallies — national regular gasoline $4.25 on Wednesday against $3.05 a year earlier, up nearly 40% (AAA, ¶5); the holder's clock restated ('come down really fast', 'very, very rapidly' — ¶7–¶8) and the cure renamed: the Venezuela energy deal, the first million barrels 'free' and refined in Texas, 65 billion barrels of reserves (¶6, ¶9–¶11). Russian diesel, the Strait, the cargo and the waiver are not on the page; the voters read the price as 'the long haul'

zAxis.pos: prices come down by the deal — soon — and the voters feel it before November 3
zAxis.neg: they do not — the pump is forty percent up on a year ago, the cure on the page now carries a different seller's name, and the audience reads the price as a cost of keeping the republic

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's promise — diesel 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11), 'come down soon' (10-24), now 'really fast' and 'very, very rapidly' at Lubbock. The page puts the pump beside it ($4.25 against $3.05, +40%) and the cure beside that — and the cure has changed its name: not Russian diesel, not the Strait, but a million Venezuelan barrels 'free to taxpayers' and 65 billion in reserves, with 'lower consumer costs expected eventually' in the administration's own clause (¶10). 'Very, very rapidly' and 'eventually' sit two paragraphs apart. The voters do not dispute the number; they read it as the long haul, and move the threat from the pump to the republic

log.what: daily cut over the 10-29 sweep (GitHub raw; no local copy, no transcripts on disk). Twenty-two paragraphs read in full via the cloud fetch; seventeen scored and two constitutive (Trump @O, the principal — declared +0.9). Object declared on H1c at the pump, the Give Him Time (10-27) precedent: the same page shape five days on, with the pump now a national figure and the cure renamed Venezuela. The holder's ballot lines (¶15–¶16) left unscored as off-object and sorted to the slate in the pass. Chosen as the newest Fox hit on the live object; one Fox cut per day; my call

split.note: one station, two planes: the article (the price dated and sized, the cure reported with its new name and its slower clock — 6–18) and the voters (the price as the long haul, then the republic, socialism, opportunity — 36–70). The voters do not dispute the article's forty percent; they relocate the threat. No migration inside one voice on the price; Trigo climbs 46 → 52 on the future and the term, off the object

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: sky-high gas prices aren't shaking the MAGA faithful in oil country; supporters warn of a bigger threat
lines.note: THE DOOR: the price is 'sky-high' and the audience 'the faithful' in one hed; the threat is already somewhere else
lines.zWhy: a sky-high pump that does not shake the faithful is a price not yet down for them

lines.quote: gas prices soaring ahead of the midterms; the rising costs aren't shaking loyalty; some warn the country's future is at stake
lines.note: the lede: the price, the vote and the relocation in one sentence
lines.zWhy: soaring before the midterms is a cure not yet arrived

lines.quote: I do experience that costs are high, but I'm in for the long haul
lines.note: THE TITLE — the gas↔votes predicate answered by patience (Texas edition of 'give him time', 10-27 ¶7); the voter grants the number and extends the clock
lines.zWhy: the long haul is a price read as temporary by the one paying it

lines.quote: Lubbock and Corpus Christi, two cities tied to oil and gas; voters acknowledge the squeeze, remain behind the president; socialism adds urgency
lines.note: the setting — oil country reading its own product's price
lines.zWhy: a squeeze acknowledged in oil country is a price up where it is produced

lines.quote: national average regular ≈$4.25 Wednesday, up nearly 40% from ≈$3.05 a year earlier (AAA)
lines.note: THE PRICE, DATED AND SIZED — the page's lowest line; a national figure where the 10-27 page had Georgia's. Gasoline, not diesel: the other leg of H1c, and the page does not mention the one the deal is for
lines.zWhy: forty percent in a year is a cure not yet at the pump

lines.quote: Trump acknowledged the higher costs; pointed to increased American oil production and the Venezuela energy deal as steps toward bringing prices down
lines.note: THE CURE RENAMED — reported: the holder's steps are production and Venezuela; Russian diesel, the cargo, the Strait are not in the sentence
lines.zWhy: a cure with a new name is the old cure not yet felt

lines.quote: our country is making a fortune while people have to pay more at the pump; gas prices are going to come down really fast
lines.note: constitutive — THE HOLDER'S CLOCK, fifth phrasing: 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11) → 'immediately' (the 300,000 t) → 'soon' (10-24, Perry) → 'really fast' (Lubbock). The fortune and the pump in one sentence — the holder states both sides of H1c himself. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: the ones we care about are our people at the pump; the numbers will fall very, very rapidly
lines.note: constitutive — the clock again, two words faster; the audience named as the object's. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: at Corpus Christi Trump announced the first million barrels of Venezuelan oil — at no cost to taxpayers per the White House, to be refined in Texas
lines.note: THE NEW CARGO: a million barrels from a different seller, 'free'. The deal's own cargo (40,000 t at sea for New York, fox 10-24) is not on the page; neither is the deal
lines.zWhy: a million barrels landed is a cure arriving — from Venezuela, not from the deal

lines.quote: the administration presents the agreement as expanding supply and supporting jobs, with lower consumer costs expected eventually
lines.note: 'EVENTUALLY' — the administration's clock for its own cure, two paragraphs from 'very, very rapidly'; the slowest phrasing on the Press
lines.zWhy: 'eventually' is a cure the office dates later than the holder

lines.quote: the broader deal would give the US majority control over about 65 billion barrels of proven Venezuelan reserves
lines.note: the cure sized as reserves, undated — supply promised, not a price moved; 'majority control' is the 10-11 'U.S. control' sentence with a new country in it
lines.zWhy: sixty-five billion barrels of control is supply promised, not a pump moved

lines.quote: the economy is my top midterm concern; Republicans can fix it
lines.note: the voter's object is 'the economy'; the price inside it, unnamed
lines.zWhy: an economy to be fixed reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: without the Republicans in charge we won't go that direction; hoping next year is better
lines.note: 'NEXT YEAR' — the voter's clock, past the election; the third clock on the page after 'really fast' and 'eventually'
lines.zWhy: next year is a cure the voter dates past November 3

lines.quote: Democrats under pressure from the progressive wing; democratic socialist candidates gaining prominence
lines.note: the article's pivot off the price — vacancy
lines.zWhy: a progressive wing reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: some concerns extend beyond affordability; socialism threatens the nation's future
lines.note: THE RELOCATION, in the article's own voice — 'beyond affordability' is the price left behind; vacancy
lines.zWhy: a threat beyond affordability is the pump no longer the object

lines.quote: we can't lose our republic; Democrats, socialists and communists are besieging the country
lines.note: the page's peak — denominated; the 'bigger threat' of the hed in a voter's mouth; vacancy
lines.zWhy: a republic to be lost reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: the midterms are about the future and the opportunities for the next generation
lines.note: the object replaced by 'the future'; vacancy
lines.zWhy: the next generation's opportunity reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: opportunity is the key issue; Trump is on the side of opportunity
lines.zWhy: a side of opportunity reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: keep fighting the war on drugs and resisting socialism over his remaining two years
lines.note: 'TWO YEARS' — the fourth clock on the page, the holder's term; the price not in it; vacancy
lines.zWhy: two years is a window with no price in it
